chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sajisi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated, from Suhayl, from Safwan, from Abu Yazid, from Al-Qa'qa' ibn al-Lajlaj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), saying:
Miserliness and faith will never coexist in the heart of a servant.
ai.seo_question: What two qualities cannot coexist in a believer's heart according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith to illustrate the spiritual incompatibility between *shuhh* (greed/miserliness) and *iman* (faith), emphasizing that true belief necessitates generosity. This narration underscores the Shia ethical view that internal character traits directly determine the authenticity of one's religious state, a concept deeply rooted in the Purification of the Soul (*Tazkiyah*).
